unit.sep: Construct and critique representations,classify structures and use evidence for material selection.
unit.careers: Illustrative materials design,manufacturing and science-communication roles.
unit.focus: Bond and bond types; Bond formation in common compounds and metals; Bond types and their structures; Uses of Diamond, Graphite and Aluminium.
unit.phenomenon: A fictional poster says every covalent substance is soft and insulating,ionic crystals are molecules,and an Al bond model certifies every cookware product.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Electron diagrams,explicit particle/structure records,safe optional solubility evidence,carbon allotropes and constrained material jobs.
unit.drivingQuestion: How do bond types relate to physical properties of compounds?
unit.content: Bond and bond types; Bond formation in common compounds and metals; Bond types and their structures; Uses of Diamond, Graphite and Aluminium.
unit.coreCompetencies:
Communication and collaboration: as the learner sensitises the community on use and care of common appliances such as utensils and other cookware.
Digital literacy: the learner navigates through online sources to access virtual laboratories for simulations on formation of chemical bonds.
Creativity and imagination: as the learner undertakes a project of modelling ball and stick ionic and covalent structures of selected molecules using locally available resources.
unit.values:
Respect: as the learner recognises and appreciates the input of every group member when discussing the relationship between bond types and physical properties of different structures.
Patriotism: as the learner sensitises the community on use and care of common appliances such as utensils and other cookware.
unit.pcis:
Safety and Security: as the learner observes safety precautions when carrying out activities to investigate properties of elements and compounds.
Financial Literacy: as the learner makes informed decisions when selecting appropriate items, appliances and equipment made from specific elements and compounds.

assessment.instructions: Independent40minutes:4readCB14,14Section1,8Section2,8Section3,6Section4/check/submit. Use only held-out reference and prompts;no teacher keys,hints or shared answers. Draw actual required representations. No performed activity is inferred from written work.

sections.title: 1. Draw bonding and an intermolecular attraction
sections.prompt: Use CB14 to draw before/after MgF2 outer-electron dot/cross representations with bracketed charges and transferred electrons. Draw two water molecules showing shared/lone pairs,partial charges and one dotted intermolecular attraction. Illustrate NH3 donating its lone pair to H+ to form NH4+;give total outer electrons and explain final bond equivalence. Label the bond/interaction types and any omitted inner shells.
sections.exemplar: Mg transfers one electron to each of two F atoms:Mg2+ and2F−,each F7dots+1cross and octet. H2O has2shared O–H pairs and2O lone pairs;Oδ−/Hδ+,dotted intermolecularO···H distinct from covalentO–H. NH3 lone pair forms a dative covalent bond toH+;NH4+ has8outer electrons and4equivalent formedN–H bonds,bracketcharge+. Drawings must actually show these features.

sections.title: 2. Structures explain properties
sections.prompt: Classify MgF2,H2O,diamond,graphite andAl by structure. Explain solid/molten MgF2 conductivity,solidAl conductivity and graphite versus diamond electrical behaviour. Use one supplied example to reject the rule that all covalent substances have low melting points.
sections.exemplar: MgF2 giantionic,H2O simplemolecular,diamond/graphite giantcovalent,Al metallic. Mobile ions conduct in moltenMgF2,not fixed solidions. Al/graphite have mobileelectrons;diamond lacks comparable carriers. Diamond network has strong extended covalent bonding,so a universal low-melting covalent rule fails. Graphite layers have strong internalbonds and weaker interlayerforces.

sections.title: 3. Material choices with conditions
sections.prompt: Using the final records,choose a material for each fictional job:solid electricalcontact,hardabrasive,formableheat-transfercontainer. Explain structure→property→use for each and state one practical limit or additional evidence needed. Do not invent costs or product certificates.
sections.exemplar: ContactAl orgraphite:mobileelectrons support conduction,subject tocontact/productcompatibility. Abrasivediamond:strong3Dnetwork giveshardness,subject tograde/application. ContainerAl:metallicstructure supportsheattransfer/forming,but actualmanufacturerinstructions,coating andstovecompatibility are needed. Noexactprice/bestoverallverdict.

sections.title: 4. Reflect on model and performance limits
sections.prompt: Explain one way considering structure and practical conditions changes a choice based only on bond type. State a precise representation limit and whether these written answers establish actual model construction,property testing,virtual-lab navigation or community delivery.
sections.exemplar: Graphite is covalent but its layers/delocalised electrons make it suitable for some contacts;bond label alone would miss that. Ball/stick sizes and boundary fragments are schematic. Written work does not establish any of the four actual activities;separate observed evidence is needed.
